newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tehran says it has arrested missing Iranian writer.
newsitem.headline: Tehran says it has arrested missing Iranian writer.

text.p: Tehran says it has arrested Faraj Sarkuhi, an Iranian journalist whose disappearance has caused concern in Germany, the Bonn Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday.
Bonn also said documents provided by Iran to prove Sarkuhi visited Germany last year -- when he says he was being tortured in detention -- were probably false.
"The good news is that the whereabouts of Sarkuhi have been cleared up," Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann told a news conference.

"But the bad news is that last night our ambassador was told that Sarkuhi had been arrested in Bushir in south-west Iran on Sunday, February 2, allegedly trying to leave the country illegally," Erdmann said.

Sarkuhi, the editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday), says Tehran is trying to use him as a pawn to counter accusations against Iran made by German prosecutors in a Kurdish dissident assassination case.
Sarkuhi was one of six Iranian writers held briefly after security agents burst into a dinner function at the home of the German cultural attache Jens Gust in July.

Tehran later expressed regret over the incident after Bonn protested the action in which the news weekly der Spiegel said the agents threatened Gust with violence, locked him in a room and interrogated him.

Germany asked Iran for details of Sarkuhi's whereabouts following reports last week that he had not only been detained and tortured for 47 days last year when he was supposedly in Germany, but had now been arrested again.
Erdmann said Bonn still wanted Iran to comment on these allegations, made in a letter from Sarkuhi which was published in several newspapers.
Sarkuhi was first reported missing last November, when he was due to fly to Germany to visit his wife. She says he never arrived, but Iran provided documents to show he did.
Erdmann told Reuters the entry stamp on these papers was "probably not real" -- backing up Sarkuhi's claim that Iran sent someone else to Germany with his passport.
On December 20, Sarkuhi appeared at Tehran airport to hold a news conference, saying he had indeed been in Germany but had not told anyone of his whereabouts for personal reasons.
But in a subsequent 14-page handwritten letter published by several newspapers, which Bonn believes is genuine, Sarkuhi said he had been forced to lie.
He said he had been held by the Iranian secret service and forced under torture to confess in a taped interview that he had spied for Germany.

He said he believed authorities intended to use the confession in a row with Germany over an accusation by German prosecutors that Iranian leaders ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin in 1992.
An Iranian and four Lebanese are being tried for the killings. Iran has denied involvement.
